mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0%, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and retail sales indicates broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when both HOUST and RSAFS decline simultaneously in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime defined by industrial production falling below 95.0, the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced economic output and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC for the regime is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 220.0, it signals elevated inflation that may prompt monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment and rise in unemployment indicates severe labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic contraction.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises simultaneously in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime defined by GDP exceeding 17000.0 billion dollars, the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to sustained economic growth and corporate earnings momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 > 17000.0, or the Rank IC for the regime is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production consistently signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
